findings.ref: staged plugins/sdd-lite/skills/lite-spec/SKILL.md 'Capability-derived signal' clause vs security-spec.md B2 row and requirements.md Security Boundaries
findings.note: The delivered producer text names exactly one condition under which the second argument may be omitted: 'If no Project Context exists at all (disabled-legacy), skip this step entirely -- no fragment is produced, and the checker below runs with its first argument only, exactly as before this extension.' It states no rule for the case where a Project Context DOES exist but the signal source fails: evaluate-predicate absent or exiting non-zero, the Registry unreadable/malformed, or the temp-fragment write failing. The unstated default is the same one-argument invocation, i.e. the legacy keyword-only path. security-spec.md's B2 row names the asset as 'input-validation integrity: a caller that attempts to supply a Capability-derived signal and fails must never be silently treated as one that never attempted to', and requirements.md says 'The only condition that legitimately degrades rather than Blocks is the second argument's own total absence.' investigation.md INV-014 explicitly places the 'upstream signal-source producer made an error' case inside this class. All enforcement delivered for that class is consumer-side (T-002's supplied-but-invalid -> exit 2, TEST-013a..g); the B2 flowchart itself models the producer as emitting only 'trigger fragment JSON, or argument omitted entirely', so the 'attempted and failed' state has no owner. T-003 is the sole producer, its Risk Rationale names 'mis-assembling the trigger fragment' as the silent-defect surface, and no delivered assertion covers it (TEST-019-static-f greps only the disabled-legacy skip clause). Result: on any Capability-evaluation failure the intake gate silently reverts to keyword-only enforcement and a Lite-ineligible Capability proceeds. Partially mitigated downstream by lite-gate's AC-030 absent-Summary FAIL, but the intake contract the security spec assigns to this task is not enforced.

findings.ref: T-003.red.log 'ok: TEST-019-defense-in-depth: ship/SKILL.md still independently invokes check-risk-upgrade at ship time' with 'Results: 1 passed, 13 failed'
findings.note: The defense-in-depth case is the sole assertion that PASSES in the RED run, in both runtimes - it discriminates nothing about this task's change, because it greps an unmodified file (ship/SKILL.md) that T-003 never touches. tasks.md Done-When requires 'RED (the Block fixture AND the defense-in-depth companion against a deliberately unextended skill text)', so the required RED for this companion does not exist. Substantively the delivered assertion also does not test what was contracted: design.md Test Strategy item 6 requires 'a companion fixture confirms the existing ship-time recheck still independently BLOCKS even when the intake-time evaluation did not flag the component in question', and Done-When restates it as 'accepted-cost restated as a tested, not merely documented, property'. What was delivered is a text-presence grep proving the recheck is still mentioned, never an execution producing a Block for an unflagged component. The contract comment presents the RED as 'every static-check failure a genuine grep miss and every functional-check failure a real input unavailable/missing-parameter symptom' without disclosing that the one passing line is the defense-in-depth companion. The 14/14 GREEN therefore overstates coverage of the OQ-002 layering property.

findings.ref: tasks.md T-003 Blocker note vs human-copy/README.md 'Canonical-path staging (current)' and apply-protected-files.ps1 header
findings.note: The frozen task contract still asserts the deliverable is 'staged as non-suffix-matching .PROPOSED content under specs/epic-194-a6-lite-integration/human-copy/PROPOSED/', while the staging README states 'There is no .PROPOSED-suffix workaround here any more' and that the session 'migrated every PROPOSED/*.PROPOSED file to its real relative path and deleted the obsolete PROPOSED/ subtree'. The runner itself now treats such a subtree as hostile: 'a nested PROPOSED/ subtree is explicitly rejected (payload, never an implicitly ignored control subtree)'. A human executing the pending HUMAN APPLY STEP from the task contract is pointed at a path that no longer exists and at a convention the runner rejects. Related: the Blocker note says 'this task cannot reach Implementation Complete in the normal sense until then', the Done-When HUMAN APPLY STEP box is unticked, and the README says 'Not a claim that T-002/T-003 are Done, or even Implementation Complete' - yet tasks.md reads 'Status: Implementation Complete'. The delivered lifecycle state of a Security-Sensitive gate task is asserted three different ways in one bundle.

findings.ref: acceptance-tests.md AC-019 vs the delivered assertion set
findings.note: AC-019 requires the Block to fire 'before any specs/<feature>/ file exists' with 'non-overridability (--lite never overrides)'. Neither property is executed by any delivered assertion: position and non-overridability are verified only as prose greps (TEST-019-static-g greps the weak anchor 'regardless of whether the'), and TEST-019-functional-a/b/c invoke check-risk-upgrade against a hand-authored fragment - i.e. they re-exercise T-002's merge contract, not any producer logic T-003 delivers. The gate's position is structurally inherited from the pre-existing section opener, so the property is plausibly satisfied, but nothing in the suite locks the new clause inside that pre-Process section against a later edit. Verifiable from the logs only; the suite source is not in the bundle.

The required regression check is recorded passes:true on a scoped substitute because 'the full 116-suite tests/run-all.sh TIMED OUT after 10 minutes and could not be completed this session'. The substitution is disclosed and precedent-matched to T-004, so this is not concealed, but a required regression gate is green without the full suite ever having completed for this task. Similarly, placeholder-scan is passes:true while 'The CHANGELOG.md whole-file scan separately FAILS on 5 pre-existing findings' (disclosed as byte-identical at merge-base bd48ce8c).
